A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forward-model analysis. Their text, equations, five figures, Appendices A–C, and checklist support reliable comparison. The additional page in v3 comes from bibliography reformatting.

before.justification: Appendix B reports original Monte Carlo simulations validating TEST, AlphaBeta, and Scout complexity predictions in Figures 3–5.

after.justification: Appendix B retains the original Monte Carlo validation results for TEST, AlphaBeta, and Scout, including estimates and confidence intervals.

M1.justification: The forward-sampling procedure and Algorithms 1–5 are unchanged. Introducing the F-game terminology and relocating the Scout footnote do not alter any procedure.

E1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix B retain the same synthetic game-tree coverage, including uniform, triangular, power-law, and bimodal-uniform distributions. F-games names the existing generated games rather than introducing new evaluation scenarios.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains AlphaBeta, Scout, TEST-BRUTEFORCE, TEST-BISECTION, and TEST-HARDEST. Appendix B retains the same Monte Carlo versus analytical-oracle comparisons.

E3.justification: Figure 2 retains b = 10 and n = 5 for finite-depth comparisons, the same height range, and the same relative leaf-evaluation metric. Appendix B preserves its parameter configurations and Monte Carlo trial counts.

E4.justification: The distribution- and depth-dependent comparisons in Figure 2 and the Monte Carlo validation analyses in Appendix B are unchanged. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix B still reports averages over five independent random seeds and bootstrapped 95% confidence intervals. Figure 2 remains a numerical calculation of expected complexities without sampling-error bars.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 contain identical plotted results. Both versions retain AlphaBeta approaching TEST-BRUTEFORCE's cost, Scout's lower cost on deep trees, and Monte Carlo estimates converging toward the analytical predictions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, recurrences, Theorems 4.1, 5.1, and 5.2, and derivations in Appendices A and C are unchanged. Adjustments to expectation subscripts and equation spacing are typesetting changes.

C1.justification: Section 1 drops the claim that AlphaBeta's extra factor is proportional to the value range, retaining only a larger factor and more leaf evaluations. It also replaces tentative branching-factor equality with a categorical statement, although Sections 5.3 and 8 still describe Scout equality as unproved.

C2.justification: Sections 6–8 retain the explanations for AlphaBeta's near-bruteforce behavior, Scout's adaptive thresholds, and the same model and algorithm limitations. The introduction's revised sibling-correlation wording reiterates the existing structural-dependency motivation.

D1.justification: Sampling pseudocode, matrix-iteration and spectral-radius computation details, and code-access information are retained. Appendix B still reports a couple of CPU hours on a consumer-grade laptop.

R1.justification: The same 24 works are cited, and Section 7 preserves the comparisons with previous models and algorithms. Reference reordering, formatting changes, and expanded author lists do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: The title and selected abstract, introduction, and discussion passages emphasize a class of synthetic games and introduce Forward-game/F-game terminology. Other edits concern local wording, punctuation, and reference style; the overall narrative structure is retained.

P2.justification: The Section 6 heading moves above Figure 2, the Scout footnote moves onto its algorithm's page, and equation spacing changes. References now occupy two pages. All figure content is retained, and the appendices are only repaginated.

improvement.justification: The methods, proofs, numerical evidence, validation, and reproducibility information remain intact. Terminology and layout receive limited cleanup. The introduction narrows the AlphaBeta overhead claim but states branching-factor equality more strongly despite the unchanged Scout proof gap; the detailed sections retain their qualifications. These localized edits leave overall evidential strength and usefulness essentially unchanged.
